subject_name: Aircraft Wiring Practices (Electrical wiring and Interface system)
topic: Auto rotation, ground resonance, vortex ring, blade sailing
syllabus_extract: Auto rotation, ground resonance, vortex ring, blade sailing.
specific_objectives: 12.1.7.1 Trainee will be able to explain auto rotation, ground resonance, vortex ring, blade sailing.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of flight simulation scenarios demonstrating auto rotation entry, ground resonance excitation, vortex ring state recovery, and blade sailing conditions. Safety: Ensure simulator controls are reset between scenarios. Instructor supervision: Monitor trainee interpretation of flight data and recovery procedures.
intro_questions: What is the primary purpose of auto rotation in helicopter flight?
Define ground resonance and identify the component most susceptible to it.
How does the rotor disc behave during vortex ring state?

development.content:
Principles of Auto Rotation
Energy conversion in descent
Control inputs during entry
Recovery procedures
Limitations of auto rotation

Ground Resonance Mechanics
Blade Sailing Phenomenon
Vortex Ring State Dynamics
Prevention and Recovery
System limitations

Comparative Analysis of Hazards
Emergency Procedures Review
Pilot Decision Making
Maintenance Implications
Operational Constraints

summary_questions: Explain the difference between ground resonance and blade sailing.
Describe the immediate pilot actions required to recover from vortex ring state.
What are the key indicators that a helicopter is entering auto rotation?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on how the principles of auto rotation apply to emergency landing procedures in LP 02.
